## Body

Lessons from the home-prefetch review cycle (dd9713a6e -> eef5899dd, 2026-11-12):

- A cache keyed on git metadata must also key on things git derives from the filesystem: `worktree list` reports a linked worktree prunable when its checkout (the path in `<common>/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`) is gone, which touches no metadata file. Include checkout existence and `locked` in the stamp.
- Never cache a failed read as a value: a non-zero git exit or a failed availability check returned [] and was remembered forever. Return a "listed/ok" flag and cache only successes; memoize capability checks only when they pass.
- Write the reviewer's repros as permanent real-git tests (UnixProcessManager + NodeFileSystemAdapter in a tmp repo, under test/integration/** so they get the process timeout bound) and prove each fails on the old commit before landing.
- Report launch counts per class (worktree list / --version / status-log-diff) and the total; "158 -> 3" hid that the total was 11 and needed a correction of record.
- A fresh worktree's `tsc -p test` fails on unbuilt packages (@chainglass/workgraph dist missing); that is environment, not code. just fft builds first.
- Rebasing uncommitted work without stash: `git diff -- <file> > p; git apply -R p; git merge --ff-only origin/main; git apply -3 p`.
